hindsight_note: Thirteen other same-way crypto legs plus a 5.5 ATR stop were visible at entry; price never got past 0.57R before failing. Crowding deserved a harsher grade than C.
Pullback short died in five bars, best excursion under 0.1R. Eleven other same-way legs and three in this market make the B too generous; the trend read alone did not justify it.
Breakout reached 0.9R then faded; strategy close banked only 0.22R after 26 bars. The far 6R target was never realistic. Marginal C stands.
Low-ADX chop breakout pushed to nearly 1R then reversed through the stop, as the blind note predicted. Skipping was the right call; grade holds.
Never showed more than 0.13R before stopping. The wide stop after a sharp prior move was the flagged weakness; the sweep and displacement did not follow through. C stands.
Half an R of progress, then stopped within four bars. Bracket was sensible for a modest-edge breakout; this is an ordinary loss, not a decision error.
Carried nearly 800 bars and closed by reconciliation at -2.9R, far past the intended stop. Low confidence and weak displacement at entry; the lifecycle failure compounds a weak setup.
Six-ATR stop for a 1.5R target was a poor payoff and the trade never exceeded 0.36R. Volume spike on the last bar was an unresolved risk. Grade holds.
Got to 0.98R, just short of the 1.5R target, then reversed to the stop over a long hold. Tiny gap with opposing exposure already open; a skip was the better action.
Chop-regime scalp with a 4.3 ATR stop failed in seven bars with 0.3R best excursion. Poor payoff structure was visible up front; grade holds.
Strategy closed a flat trade at a small loss, symmetric 0.58R excursions each way. Low-ADX breakout offered no edge and no trend developed; skipping would have saved the cost.
Stop under 0.4 ATR was still untradeable at entry; the small net gain came from a path that ran 3.5R against and 10R for, so the drawn bracket was not the realised one. Win is not evidence.
Aligned trend with strong ADX went almost straight up; strategy close captured most of the 1.8R excursion. Stop was oversized but never tested. The win does not lift the grade.
Target hit in two bars for just 0.16R net, but price came within a hair of the 0.58 ATR stop first. Costs eat most of a sub-0.6 ATR scalp; a survived near-miss, grade holds.
Paid 23R on a 0.45 ATR stop, yet the path ran 2.3R against before working, so the stop as drawn was not what protected it. A lucky outlier on a low-confidence, tiny-gap setup.
Drifted for 132 bars with a 0.17R best excursion and was closed by reconciliation near flat. Weak confidence and a five-ATR stop never gave the trade a chance to matter.
A 0.34 ATR stop against a 15R target in chop stays unplayable; the small gain after a 12R excursion shows the stop was noise-level and the exit left the move. Do not reward the high confidence score.
Sub-0.3 ATR stop exited in one bar with a marginal gain after reaching 1.2R of the 1.5R target. Bracket is within noise either way; a coin flip, not a good decision.
Target hit for 9R but price first ran 4.7R beyond the 0.37 ATR stop, so the drawn bracket did not govern the trade. Entry geometry was unusable; the result is not a validation of it.
No follow-through at all, best excursion 0.07R, in a volatile tape with a long-heavy book. The positive news read did not translate; the wide stop made the loss clean at over 1R.
Closed after one bar by reconciliation at -0.89R with only -0.58R excursion, so the bracket did not decide it. Little can be read about the decision from the path.
A one-bar close booked -26R on a trade whose gross excursion was only -0.2R: a cost or fill artifact, not a verdict on the entry. Grade left at the blind value; flag the row as data noise.
Trend breakout ran to 8.8R with shallow drawdown but was closed by netting at 4.0R, handing back half. Entry structure matched the B; the exit path, not the decision, left money behind.
Target hit in three bars; best excursion was only 1.24R, so a further target would not have paid. The stop was nearly touched first, a reminder that the near target was not costly here.
Clean short with shallow drawdown that took the 1.5R target and then kept going to over 5R. Entry was standard and fine; the bracket left room, but a 1.5R scalp target is by design.
Low-confidence pullback got to 0.9R then rolled over to the stop. Reasonable payoff for the edge; an ordinary loss at roughly the odds expected.
Strategy closed after a single bar at a small loss before the trade could develop. Strong trend and wide trailing target at entry still look sound; one bar reveals nothing.
Reconciliation closed it after one bar at -1.15R even though gross excursion stayed within 0.16R either way. Loss came from the close mechanism, not the setup; grade unchanged.
Never moved in favour, best excursion 0.005R, with eleven same-way legs and an opposing position in this market already on. High confidence ignored the crowding; grade holds.
Strategy exit after one bar essentially flat. Chop, a 4.8 ATR stop and a crowded book were the known flaws, none tested by the path. Grade stays at the marginal blind value.
Gained 5.7R on a 0.67 ATR initial stop, but the path went 2.6R against, so the stop was not binding as drawn. Noise-level stop on a trailing trade; the gain is not credit for the setup.
Target banked after a long hold with a near-stop drawdown on the way. Strong trend, high conviction and a modest target were as described; the path was uncomfortable but the call was sound.
Exit near the stop left most of an 8.5R run. Still a sub-0.7 ATR stop with a tiny gap and a reduce news read at entry; the exit result is path luck, not support for the setup.
Stale sweep, negligible gap and low confidence; the trade barely reached 0.2R in 28 bars before the stop. The early entry on weak displacement is exactly what failed.
Three-bar stop-out after 0.8R of progress on a compact scalp with light exposure. Setup quality was as graded; at a 0.42 win probability this is a normal loser.
Closed after one bar at a modest loss. Small gap, a 3.9 ATR stop and opposing exposure in the same market were the flaws at entry, and nothing in the path argues for raising it.
Chop breakout with very low ADX stopped in three bars after a 0.7R poke. The strategy's high conviction did not make up for absent trend evidence; grade holds.
Large gap short in a volatile chop tape stopped out with little favourable excursion. Thirteen offsetting long legs were on, so crowding was not the issue. Edge was marginal as graded.
Low-ADX chop breakdown with a far 5.7R target failed in four bars at 0.2R best. Same weak trend evidence I marked down on other chop breakouts, so the C was inconsistent.
A short that ran 10.6R and exited via a trailed stop for +6.4R over 500 bars. The path survived 2.8R of heat past the stop as drawn. Chop, twelve same-way legs and a wide stop remain flaws at entry.
Closed for a small loss inside the stop, with excursions of about 0.4R each way. Trend, calm tape and positive news were fine; the wide stop never mattered. No new information on the call.
Held 353 bars and lost nearly 2R, beyond the drawn stop, with a best excursion of 0.8R. Volatile chop with a 6.3 ATR stop for a 1.5R target was a poor payoff from the start.
Target hit with shallow drawdown, excursion reaching 2.3R. Stale sweep made the entry late but the trend and calm tape carried it. A modest win consistent with the C.
Paid 17R in five bars on a 0.59 ATR stop, but price went 2.2R against first, so the stop was not binding as drawn. Chop with a tiny gap; an outlier win that does not repair the setup.
Strategy closed after one bar for a negligible gain. The short against recent upward bars was the stated worry, but one bar tells nothing about it. C stays.
Thirteen other same-way legs, a stale sweep and a 6.3 ATR stop for a 1.5R target; the trade never got beyond 0.2R. High confidence should not have offset that stacking, so the C was too kind.
One-bar strategy close for a small gain after a 0.7R adverse tick. Balanced bracket and moderate conviction at entry; the path is too short to grade the exit.
Strong-ADX short that never got above 0.23R before stopping; adverse move ran past two R, so the drawn stop was exceeded. Setup looked fine at entry and failed cleanly; grade unchanged.
A reduce news read plus a 5.9 ATR stop for a 1.5R target; the trade barely moved in favour and stopped at about -1R. Both flags were visible at entry, so the D holds.
One-bar strategy close at about +1R although the path dipped beyond the stop first. The gain says little about the pullback short's merit; a marginal-edge C stays.
